about: Story Time. level: 0 = LKG, -1 = UKG, 1-5 = Class. {name} = the child's name. Actor = [emoji, x%, y% (feet), size % of width, animation (bob hop fly walk shake grow spin float flip gold)]. Quiz answer 'a' must be one of the options 'o'.

pages.text: Hop, hop! This is Bunny.
Bunny is hungry.
Bunny finds one, two, three carrots!
Here comes Duck. Duck is hungry too.
Bunny shares a carrot with Duck. Yum! Friends share.

quiz.q: Who is this story about?
What did Bunny find?
Who did Bunny share with?

pages.text: {name} has a big red balloon.
Whoosh! The wind blows.
The balloon flies up, up, up!
A kind bird brings it back.
Thank you, bird! {name} is happy.

quiz.q: What colour is the balloon?
What blew the balloon away?
Who brought the balloon back?

pages.text: It was a hot, hot day. A crow was very thirsty.
The crow saw a pot. There was a little water at the bottom.
Its beak could not reach the water. Oh no!
The crow had an idea! It dropped pebbles into the pot, one by one.
Plop, plop, plop! The water came up and up.
The crow drank the water and flew away happily. Think and try!

quiz.q: What did the crow want?
What did the crow drop into the pot?
How did the crow feel at the end?

pages.text: A little ant went to the river to drink water.
Splash! The ant fell into the water. Help, help!
A dove saw the ant. She dropped a leaf into the river.
The ant climbed onto the leaf and floated to the land. Safe!
One day, a hunter wanted to catch the dove.
The ant bit the hunter's foot. Ouch! The dove flew away.
Friends help each other.

quiz.q: Who fell into the water?
What did the dove drop to help?
Who saved the dove?

pages.text: A big lion was sleeping under a tree in the forest.
A little mouse ran over the lion's nose. The lion woke up and caught the mouse!
"Please let me go," said the mouse. "One day I will help you." The lion laughed, but he let the mouse go.
A few days later, the lion was caught in a hunter's net. He roared and roared.
The mouse heard the roar. She ran to the lion and cut the net with her sharp teeth.
The lion was free! "Thank you, little friend," he said.
Even a small friend can be a big help.

quiz.q: Where was the lion sleeping?
What caught the lion?
How did the mouse help the lion?

pages.text: Grandma gave {name} a tiny seed.
{name} put the seed in a pot of soil and gave it water.
Every day, the sun gave it light and warmth.
One morning, a small green shoot popped out!
The plant grew taller and taller. New leaves came out.
Then a beautiful flower opened! A bee came to say hello.
Plants need soil, water, air and sunlight to grow.

quiz.q: What did Grandma give?
What came out of the soil first?
What do plants need to grow?

pages.text: Hare was very fast, and he liked to show off. "Nobody can beat me!" he said.
Tortoise said slowly, "Let us have a race." All the animals laughed.
The race began! Hare ran very fast, and soon he was far ahead.
"Tortoise is so slow," thought Hare. "I will take a nap under this tree."
Tortoise kept walking. Step by step, slow and steady, he never stopped.
Hare woke up and ran as fast as he could. But Tortoise had already crossed the finish line!
Slow and steady wins the race.

quiz.q: Who was faster?
Why did Hare lose the race?
What is the lesson of the story?
quiz.a: Slow and steady wins the race
o: Slow and steady wins the race
Never take part in a race

pages.text: A monkey lived on a jamun tree by the river. He ate sweet jamuns every day.
A crocodile lived in the river. The monkey gave him jamuns, and they became good friends.
The crocodile's wife said, "The monkey eats sweet jamuns. His heart must be sweet too. Bring it to me!"
The crocodile said, "Friend, come to my home for dinner." The monkey sat on his back.
In the middle of the river, the crocodile said, "My wife wants to eat your heart!"
The clever monkey said, "Oh no! I left my heart on the tree. Take me back and I will bring it."
Back at the river bank, the monkey jumped up the tree. "Nobody keeps a heart on a tree! Goodbye!"
Stay calm and think fast when you are in trouble.

quiz.q: Which fruit did the monkey eat?
What did the crocodile's wife want?
How did the monkey save himself?

stories.title: The Goose with the Golden Eggs

pages.text: A poor farmer and his wife had a goose. One morning, they saw something shining in its nest.
It was an egg made of pure gold! The farmer sold it and bought food for his family.
Every day the goose laid one golden egg. Slowly, the farmer became rich.
But the farmer became greedy. "Why wait every day?" he said. "I want all the eggs at once!"
He chased the goose and squeezed it hard, trying to get all the eggs out together.
The frightened goose flapped its wings and flew far, far away. It never came back.
Now the farmer had no goose and no golden eggs. He was very sorry.
Greed can make us lose what we already have.

quiz.q: What was special about the goose?
Why did the farmer lose the goose?
What does 'greedy' mean?

pages.text: On Saturday, {name} went to the park. There was plastic and paper everywhere!
Beep beep! A friendly robot rolled up. "Hello {name}! I am Robo. Will you help me clean the park?"
Robo showed two bins. "The green bin is for wet waste, like fruit peels. The blue bin is for dry waste, like paper and plastic."
{name} put the banana peels in the green bin, and the bottles and paper in the blue bin.
"Wet waste can become compost to feed plants," said Robo. "Plastic and paper can be recycled into new things!"
Soon the park was clean. The birds came back, and children played happily.
Reduce, reuse and recycle. Keep our Earth clean!

quiz.q: Which bin should banana peels go in?
What can wet waste become?
What does 'recycle' mean?
quiz.a: Making new things from old things
o: Making new things from old things

pages.text: One cold winter, Emperor Akbar said, "Who can stand in the icy lake all night? I will give a big reward."
A poor man agreed. He stood in the freezing water all night long, shivering.
In the morning Akbar asked, "How did you do it?" The man said, "I looked at a lamp burning far away in the palace."
"So the lamp kept you warm! No reward for you," said Akbar. The poor man went to Birbal, very sad.
The next day, Birbal did not come to court. Akbar went to find him. Birbal was cooking khichdi, with the pot hanging high above a tiny fire!
"How can it cook so far from the fire?" laughed Akbar. Birbal smiled. "The same way a lamp far away kept that man warm!"
Akbar understood his mistake and gave the poor man his reward. A wise answer can fix an unfair rule.

quiz.q: Where did the poor man stand all night?
Why could Birbal's khichdi not cook?
quiz.a: The fire was too far away
o: The fire was too far away

quiz.q: What did Birbal want Akbar to understand?
quiz.a: A far-away lamp cannot give warmth
o: A far-away lamp cannot give warmth

pages.text: {name} put on a space suit and climbed into the rocket. 3, 2, 1... Blast off!
The rocket zoomed up through the clouds and into space.
Earth looked like a big blue-and-green ball. In space, {name} floated! There is no air in space, so the suit gives oxygen to breathe.
After three days, the rocket landed on the Moon. The ground was grey and dusty, with big round holes called craters.
{name} jumped really high! The Moon's gravity is weaker, so you weigh only about one-sixth of your weight on Earth.
The sky was black even in the daytime, because the Moon has no air to spread the sunlight.
{name} planted a flag and waved at Earth. "I'll be back!" Then the rocket flew home.

quiz.q: What are the big holes on the Moon called?
Why could {name} jump so high on the Moon?
Why is the Moon's sky black in the daytime?

pages.text: One summer there was very little rain. Tenali Raman's garden was dry, and pulling water from the well was hard work.
One night, Tenali spotted some thieves hiding behind the bushes, waiting to rob his house.
Tenali had a smart idea. He said loudly to his wife, "Thieves are about! Let us hide our box of gold coins in the well."
They filled a heavy box with stones and dropped it into the well. Splash! The thieves heard everything.
All night long, the thieves pulled up bucket after bucket of water to reach the box. The water flowed into the garden.
By morning, the whole garden was watered! When the thieves finally reached the box, it was full of stones.
Tenali laughed, "Thank you for watering my garden!" The tired thieves ran away and never came back. Brains are stronger than muscles.

quiz.q: Why was Tenali's garden dry?
What was really inside the box?
Who watered Tenali's garden?

pages.text: In the morning there was a puddle outside school. By afternoon it was gone! "Where did the water go?" {name} wondered.
Detective {name} started the case. The Sun's heat had turned the water into invisible water vapour. This is called evaporation.
The vapour rose high into the cool sky. There it cooled and turned into tiny droplets that made clouds. This is condensation.
The droplets in the clouds joined together and became heavy. Then they fell as rain. This is precipitation.
The rain filled rivers, lakes and oceans, and soaked into the ground. This is called collection.
Then the Sun heated the water again, and everything started all over! {name} had found the water cycle.
Case closed! Water keeps moving in a cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.

quiz.q: What is evaporation?
Clouds form during…
Which order is right?
